notes_for_editor: Height conflict, not resolved: the record says 24.4 m (80 ft); the 1924 Altoona Tribune item says sixty feet (about 18.3 m). The tower may have changed between 1924 and today, so neither is proven for the current tower. Build date 1921, Aermotor design, the 2018 replacement and the 703 m elevation are not supported by any page we could read. The ArcGIS StoryMap 'Fire Towers of Pennsylvania' (storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/ed47c97ebe7246868ce8ef3e7139a0b4) appears in search results with a summary saying 'Built in 1921 by the Aermotor Windmill Company' and 'replaced in 2018', but our cached copy has no readable text, so that claim is not used as a source here. A person should open the StoryMap and check the build and replacement dates. The 1924 elevation of 2,300 ft is about 701 m, close to the record's 703 m. The WHYY and NPR 2019 articles on the new towers mention the Moshannon district but not Sandy Ridge, so they are not cited.
